source_conversation.content: I'm on an iPhone. My doctor wants my allergies and medicines to be easy for paramedics to find if I pass out. How do I set that up?

candidates.decision_basis: The user states an iPhone, so the Apple Medical ID steps apply, including the Share During Emergency Call condition and the Emergency Calls & SOS note. The Android ref is inapplicable and only serves as the marked distractor.
candidates.target:
Here is how to set up Medical ID on your iPhone so paramedics can find it.
1. Open the **Health** app and tap the **Summary** tab.
2. Tap your profile picture in the upper corner.
3. Tap **Medical ID**.
4. Turn on **Show When Locked** to make Medical ID available from the Lock screen.
5. Turn on **Share During Emergency Call** to share it with emergency responders. It is then shared automatically when you call or text emergency services from iPhone or Apple Watch.
6. Tap **Edit** or **Add** next to a field, such as medications, allergies, or conditions, to update it.
7. Tap **Done**.
If you turn off **Emergency Calls & SOS**, your Medical ID information will not be shared. That setting is under Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services.
candidates.author_note: Covers Show When Locked, Share During Emergency Call, the automatic sharing on calls and texts, the Emergency Calls & SOS condition with its location path, and the field editing steps. No iOS version is stated on the page. Enhanced Emergency Data is not available in all countries or regions; this is not stated to the user.
